title: Season 2, Ep 8: The unified tools catalog
oneliner: Stop hand-wrapping (manually describing) every API in prompts: MCP auto-translates your existing REST and OpenAPI services into LLM-callable tools, and the unified catalog makes them one governed library.
says: Application teams building agent and GenAI projects must write instructions for LLMs - prompt wrapping - which takes a lot of time. Instead, use the Model Context Protocol: it acts as an auto-translator, converting existing REST APIs and OpenAPI standards into a form LLMs understand easily, building a tool catalog or library. Application teams then connect to the unified tool catalog instead of wrapping tools by hand.
explained: The waste being eliminated: every team manually describing its APIs to the model - writing prompt text that explains what each endpoint does, its parameters, its errors. It is slow, inconsistent, and rots (becomes outdated) the moment the API changes. MCP replaces the hand-translation with a standard: APIs described once, in OpenAPI-style contracts, become tools the model can discover and call directly.

The unified catalog is the season's closing piece because it completes the loop: the MCP hub (Ep 2) centralizes connections, tenancy (Ep 3) isolates consumers, prompts (Ep 4) are governed, agents are built on one SDK (Ep 5), retrieval is a service (Ep 6), evaluation gates quality (Ep 7) - and now the tools agents may use live in one catalog with owners and policies. An enterprise agent platform, assembled episode by episode.
takeaway: The catalog finishes the platform: every tool an agent may call, translated by MCP from your existing APIs, governed in one place.
